Muktasari:
- Mchezo huo uliahirishwa Jumamosi, Machi 8, 2025 baada ya bodi ya Ligi kutangaza mda mchache kabla ya kuchezwa pambano hilo kwenye uwanja wa Mkapa, Dar es Salaam.
Kushindwa kupigwa kwa pambano la Dabi ya Kariakoo Jumamosi iliyopita kwenye Uwanja wa Benjamin Mkapa, Dar es Salaam bado ni gumzo, huku wadau mbalimbali wakilia hasara walizopata kutokana na kuahirishwa kwa pambano hilo kulikofanywa na Bodi ya Ligi.
Bodi ya Ligi iliahirisha mchezo huo saa chache kabla ya kupigwa saa 1:15 usiku baada ya awali Simba kutoa taarifa ya kugomea mchezo huo kwa sababu ya kuzuiwa kufanya mazoezi ya mwisho Kwa Mkapa kulikofanywa na wanaodaiwa makomandoo wa Yanga. Katika taarifa ya kuahirishwa kwa mchezo huo, Bodi ya Ligi ilijikanganya kwani kanuni za kuahirishwa mchezo zimetajwa katika Kanuni za Ligi Namba 34 na hakuna hata moja iliyoainisha timu ikiwa imezuiwa kufanya mazoezi mchezo hautachezwa.
Hata hivyo, licha ya mamlaka ya soka kuchukulia poa uamuzi huo wa kuiahirisha mechi hiyo ya watani wa jadi, Simba na Yanga, lakini ukweli wadau mbalimbali wakiwamo mashabiki waliosafiri umbali mrefu kutoka mikoani na wengine kutoka nje ya nchi wamelia kupata hasara kubwa.
Pia wapo wafanyabiashara na wajasiriamali ambao huitumia mechi ya watani kupiga fedha kujikuta wakila hasara ambao hakuna wa kuwalipa, ilihali Yanga waliokuwa wenyeji wakijifungia tangu jana ili kufanya tathmini ya hasara iliyopata klabu katika maandalizi ya mchezo huo wa Ligi Kuu.
Yanga imedaiwa inaandaa barua hiyo huku wakisikilizia Bodi ya Ligi inayodaiwa ilikuwa ikijiandaa kukutana kwa ajili ya kupanga tarehe mpya ya mchezo huo, ambao tayari klabu huiyo imeshasema haitacheza na wamepanga kwenda kudai haki hiyo, Mahakama ya Kimataifa ya Usuluhishi wa Michezo (CAS) kutokana na kuahirishwa kwa pambano hilo bila kuzingatia kanuni zilizopo.
Licha ya kwamba hakuna uthibitisho wa moja kwa moja juu ya hasara ya kifedha zilizojulikana kwa kuahirishwa kwa pambano hilo kuanzia Yanga yenyewe, Simba iliyougomea mchezo mapema kabla ya kuahirishwa kwake na hata mamlaka za kosa, lakini wadau wengine wamefunguka hasara walizopata, huku wakitoa lawama kwa kupuuzwa kwa mashabiki wa soka waliosafiri ili kuja kuishuhudia mechi.
MASKAUTI WA SWEDEN
Kabla ya pambano hilo kuahirishwa kulikuwepo na ujio wa maskauti wawili kutoka Sweden waliotaka kulishuhudia pambano hilo ili kumsoma vyema Clement Mzize aliyechangia kuwaleta nchini. Hata hivyo, kushindwa kufanyika kwa pambano hilo, maskauti hao wameshindwa kujizuia na kueleza hasara walizopata na kushindwa kwao kumuona Mzize wanayempigia hesabu kumtafutia dili nje kutokana na kiwango alichonacho kwa sasa.
Maskauti hao Jamal Osman na Nahom Tesfaye, walioondoka nchini jana Jumatatu, walisema kuikosa dabi kumegharimu zaidi ya milioni 20 (dola 7,619), zilizotumika katika safari kutoka Sweden hadi Tanzania. Gharama hizo zinajumuisha chakula, usafiri na malazi.
Osman na Tesfaye walikuja Tanzania kwa matumaini makubwa ya kumtazama Mzize katika mechi ya presha dhidi ya Simba, lakini hali ilibadilika ghafla kufuatia vurugu ambazo zilitokea siku moja kabla ya mchezo huo, jambo ambalo liliwafanya Simba kususia mchezo huo.
“Tulijipanga kwa muda mrefu, tukaacha kazi nyingine ili tumuangalie Mzize kwenye mechi kubwa. Sasa tumeondoka bila kufanikisha lengo letu,” alisema Osman kwa masikitiko akiwa Uwanja wa Ndege wa Kimataifa wa Julius Nyerere (JNIA).
Tesfaye aliongeza: “Tumepoteza muda na pesa nyingi, lakini haya ni mambo ya mpira. Tunapaswa kusonga mbele.”
Licha ya kuondoka bila kumwona Mzize uwanjani, maskauti hao wamesema bado wataendelea kufuatilia maendeleo yake.
“Tutajaribu kumfuatilia kwa njia zingine, lakini nafasi hii ilikuwa bora zaidi kwetu,”€ alisema Osman.
Kuondoka kwa maskauti hao ni pigo kwa Mzize, ambaye alikuwa na fursa ya kujionyesha moja kwa moja kwa wadau wa soka la Ulaya. Sasa, itabidi asubiri nafasi nyingine kuthibitisha ubora wake mbele ya maskauti wa kimataifa.
VIBANDA UMIZA
Kuahirishwa kwa dabi hiyo hakujaleta hasara kwa maskauti wa Sweden tu, bali hata wamiliki wa vibanda umiza waliowekeza fedha nyingi kuandaa mazingira ya kutazama mechi hiyo maarufu.
Maelfu ya mashabiki walikuwa wamejitayarisha kwa pambano hilo kwa kutenga fedha za tiketi na wale ambao hawakupata nafasi ya kwenda uwanjani walikuwa wamepanga kufuatilia mechi hiyo kwenye vibanda umiza vilivyojaa kila kona ya jiji la Dar es Salaam na miji mingine mikubwa.
Hata hivyo, tangazo la ghafla la kuahirishwa kwa mchezo huo liliwashtua wamiliki wa vibanda hivyo, ambao wapo ambao walikuwa tayari wamekodi televisheni kubwa, kuongeza viti na hata kuagiza vinywaji na vyakula vya kutosha kuhudumia wateja wao.
Mmoja wa wamiliki wa vibanda umiza eneo la Kinyerezi, Juma Athumani, alisema alitumia zaidi ya 150,000 kuboresha eneo lake, lakini hakufanikiwa kurudisha hata robo ya gharama hizo baada ya mechi hiyo kutofanyika.
“Nilikodi ‘screen’ kubwa na kununua spika mpya ili mashabiki wa Yanga na Simba wafurahie mechi, lakini sasa kila kitu kimeharibika. Pesa zimepotea bure,” alisema, huku mmiliki mwingine wa kibanda umiza eneo la Mabibo, alisema alilipia king’amuzi za Azam sambamba na kununua vinywaji kwa ajili ya kuviuza wakati wa mechi hiyo, lakini kila kitui kimeenda sivyo na hajui wa kumpungizia machungu.
“Ni kweli hata kama mechi imeahirishwa, vinywaji na king’amuzi bado zitabaki, lakini haikuwa lengo langu kutumia fedha za ziada kwa maandalizi ya mchezo huo na unajua vipato vyetu watanzania ni vya kuungaunga, unatoa fedha kimahesabu ili kuvuna faida, lakini mambo yamenichachia. Inaumiza.”
WAJASIRIAMALI
Shabiki kindakindaki wa Yanga anayejulikana kwa jina la Jesca Manji, amesema kitendo cha dabi ya Yanga na Simba kuahirishwa Machi 8 kimemuingiza katika madeni yaliyotaka kusababisha ajidhuru.
Jesca anayejishughulisha na biashara ya kuuza vyakula (mama lishe) aliliambia Mwanaspoti alikwenda kuchukua kuku kwa mtu kwa mali kauli, alitegemea baada ya dabi anakwenda kupeleka pesa za watu, lakini mambo yakaenda sivyo. “Nilichukua kuku wa Sh2 milioni na nilifanya maandalizi ya biashara kila kitu kikawa tayari, ajabu bodi ya Ligi Kuu Tanzania ikatoa taarifa saa 8:00 mchana hakuna mechi, nikajikuta naishiwa nguvu, nashindwa cha kufanya, kwa sababu mwenye kuku anataka pesa zake siyo maneno,” alisema Jesca na kuongeza;
“Nakajikuta natamani kunywa dawa ili nife, lakini kitu kilichonipa nguvu ni mama ninayelea watoto wangu mwenyewe, nikawaza nikiondoka duniani wataishi vipi, nikapata nguvu ya kuendelea kupambana kuona ni namna gani nitalipa deni la watu.”
Alisema kwa biashara ya aina yake kama hana friji la kuhifadhia kuku wanaharibika na ndicho kilichotokea kwa watu wengi Machi 8, ambao wakajikuta wanatupa vyakula. “TFF na Bodi ya Ligi wangefikiria kwa mapana katika uamuzi wao, wanajua kuna wafanye biashara wanawake ambao wanapambania maisha yao, acha ninyamaze maana nina hasira nashindwa cha kufanya,” alisema Jesca.
Wachuuzi wengine kando ya Uwanja wa Mkapa, walisema walitegemea kutengeneza pesa ya ziada kupitia dabi kama inavyokuwepo siku zote kukiwa na mechi kubwa, lakini wamejikuta wakipata hasara ya vyakula bila kujua wa kuwalipa gharama hizo.
“Inauma sana watu wachache wanafanya mambo kwa utashi wao, bila kujali hasara inayopatikana kwa waliopo nyuma ya mchezo mkubwa kama huo, ni kuwakosea heshima mashabiki na mpira wa miguu kwa ujumla, kwani nasikia hakuna kanuni za kuahirisha zilizotumika, ila maamuzi ya kulindana tu, hii sio sawa na inarudisha nyuma uchumi wa mtu mmoja mmoja na hata taifa kwa ujumla,” alisema Hellen Muro mama ntilie.
WA MIKOANI NAO
Getruda Emmanuel kutoka Mafinga, alisema Dabi hii imejua kuwakomesha kwani walisafiri kutoka Mafinga hadi Dar es Salaam kwa usafiri wa gari mbili aina ya coaster ambazo walikodi wakiwa mashabiki jumla 60 na kila mmoja alilipa nauli kiasi cha shilini 60,000 ya kwenda na kurudi.
Mbali na nauli, Getruda amebainisha kuwa alilipia sehemu ya kulala kwa siku mbili huku kila siku ikiwa ni shilingi 20,000.
“Sisi tumechangishana kila mmoja ametoa shilingi 60,000 ya nauli kwenda na kurudi, tulikodi gari mbili ambapo tulikuwa mashabiki 60. Ukiangalia gharama za kukodi gari zote hizo nauli jumla shilingi milioni tatu na laki sita,” alisema Getrude.
Getrude alisema kwa upande wake jumla alitumia zaidi ya Shilingi 150,000 ikiwemo usafiri, kula, kulala pamoja na kununua jezi.
“Achana na gharama hizo, pia mimi ni mfanyabiashara, nimelazimika kufunga biashara yangu kwa siku mbili kwa ajili ya kuja kuiangalia mechi hii, hivyo sijaingiza kitu na nilichokifuata nimekikosa,” alisema Getrude na kuongeza.
“Kutokana na haya yanayoendelea, sidhani kama wakati mwingine mashabiki kutoka mikoani tutakuja kuangalia mechi hizi za dabi au mechi yoyote kubwa, kwani imekuwa haina uhakika kama inachezwa kwani unaweza kujiandaa ukifika hamna mechi.”
YANGA SASA
Mwanaspoti liliutafuta uongozi wa Yanga kutaka kujua hasara iliyopata klabu hiyo iliyokuwa wenyeji, lakini simu zao zilikuwa zikiita bila kupokelewa, ila chanzo cha ndani kutoka klabuni alilidokeza Mwanaspoti kuwa, viongozi walikuwa wakijadiliana na kufanya tathmini ya jambo hilo.
“Huwezi kuwapata kwa sasa, kwani wanajadiliana na kufanya tathmini ya pamoja ya kujua hasara nzima ili kuwekwa kwenye barua ya kisheria itakayotumwa CAS, ili kudai pointi tatu za mchezo huo wa Machi 8 kama ilivyoainishwa kwenye taarifa kwa umma,” kilisema chanzo hicho na kuongeza;
“Kuna gharama kubwa zilizopatikana kuanzia maandalizi ya kambi, matangazo na mambo mengine, hivyo sio rahisi kufahamika, ndio maana wanakutana kwa sasa kuweka sawa kisha watatoa taarifa, ila ukweli ni kwamba Yanga imepata hasara za mamilioni ya fedha kwa sababu ya ubinafsi wa wachache.”
Mapema Ofisa Habari wa Yanga, Ally Kamwe alikaririwa kwamba kabla ya mechi kuahirishwa tayari tiketi zaidi ya 40,000 zilizokuwa zimeuzwa kwa mashabiki, ambao hata hivyo hawakupata nafasi ya kulishuhudia pambano hilo kutokana na kuahirishwa na Bodi ya Ligi baada ya tishio la Simba kugoma.
Maofisa wa Simba na wale wa Bodi ya Ligi walipotafutwa ili kupata ufafanuzi wa hasara ambazo walipata katika maandalizi ya mchezo huo kabla ya kuahirishwa muda mchache hazikuzaa matunda kwani simu zilikuwa zikiitwa bila kupokelewa.
Bodi ya Ligi ndio wasimamizi wakuu wa mchezo huo, wakibeba gharama za kuwahudumia maofisa wa mchezo huo wakiwamo waamuzi, kamisaa na wengine iwe ni kutoka Dar es Salaam au mikoani. Hii ni mara ya 13 kwa Simba na Yanga kukachana kwa sababu mbalimbali katika mechi za Ligi ya Bara tangu ligi hiyo ilipoasisiwa mwaka 1965, huku rekodi zikionyesha Simba inaongoza kwa kufanya hivyo mara saba dhidi ya sita za watani wao na kwa miaka karibuni hii ni mara ya pili kwa dabi kuahirishwa ndani ya muda mfupi ikiwamo lile la Mei 8 mwaka 2021 na Yanga iligoma kucheza. Mechi hiyo ya Mei 8, ilipangiwa kuchezwa upya Julai 3, mwaka huo na Yanga kushinda kwa bao 1-0 lililowekwa kimiani na Zawadi Mauya, huku mchezo ulioahirishwa wikiendi bado haujapangiwa muda na tayari Yanga imesisitiza haitaucheza kwani ilishamaliza kazi Machi 8.

Summary:
- The match was postponed on Saturday, March 8, 2025 after the League Board announced it shortly before the fixture was due to be played at the Mkapa stadium in Dar es Salaam.

The failure to play the Kariakoo Derby last Saturday at the Benjamin Mkapa Stadium in Dar es Salaam is still the talk of the town, with various stakeholders lamenting the losses they suffered as a result of the match being postponed by the League Board.

The League Board postponed the match a few hours before it was due to kick off at 1:15 in the evening (19:15), after Simba had earlier issued a statement boycotting the match because they had been prevented from holding their final training session at the Mkapa stadium by people alleged to be Yanga "commandos". In its statement announcing the postponement, the League Board contradicted itself, because the rules for postponing a match are set out in League Regulation No. 34 and none of them states that if a team has been prevented from training the match will not be played.

However, even though the football authorities took the decision to postpone the match between the traditional rivals Simba and Yanga lightly, the truth is that various stakeholders, including fans who travelled long distances from the regions and others from outside the country, have complained of suffering big losses.

There are also traders and entrepreneurs who use the derby to make money and who found themselves making losses with no one to compensate them, while Yanga, who were the hosts, had been locked in session since yesterday in order to assess the losses the club incurred in preparing for this Premier League match.

Yanga is said to be preparing that letter while listening out for the League Board, which is said to have been preparing to meet in order to set a new date for the match - a match the club has already said it will not play, having decided to go and demand its rights at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) because of the postponement of the fixture without regard to the existing regulations.

Although there is no direct confirmation of the financial losses caused by the postponement from Yanga itself, from Simba, which boycotted the match before it was postponed, or even from the authorities at fault, other stakeholders have spoken out about the losses they suffered, while blaming the disregard shown to football fans who travelled to come and watch the match.

SCOUTS FROM SWEDEN

Before the match was postponed, two scouts from Sweden had arrived wanting to watch the fixture in order to take a good look at Clement Mzize, who was the reason they came to the country. However, with the match failing to take place, the scouts could not contain themselves and spoke of the losses they suffered and their failure to see Mzize, whom they are counting on to find a deal abroad because of the level he is at now.

The scouts, Jamal Osman and Nahom Tesfaye, who left the country yesterday, Monday, said that missing the derby cost them more than 20 million shillings (7,619 dollars) spent on the trip from Sweden to Tanzania. Those costs include food, transport and accommodation.

Osman and Tesfaye came to Tanzania with high hopes of watching Mzize in a high-pressure match against Simba, but the situation changed suddenly following the chaos that occurred a day before the match, which caused Simba to boycott it.

"We planned for a long time, we set aside other work so that we could watch Mzize in a big match. Now we have left without achieving our goal," said Osman with regret at Julius Nyerere International Airport (JNIA).

Tesfaye added: "We have lost a lot of time and money, but these are football matters. We have to move on."

Despite leaving without seeing Mzize on the pitch, the scouts said they will still continue to follow his progress.

"We will try to follow him by other means, but this opportunity was the best for us," said Osman.

The departure of the scouts is a blow to Mzize, who had the chance to showcase himself directly to European football stakeholders. Now he will have to wait for another opportunity to prove his quality before international scouts.

SPORTS-VIEWING KIOSKS

The postponement of the derby did not only bring losses to the Swedish scouts, but also to the owners of the sports-viewing kiosks who had invested a lot of money preparing the setting for watching this famous match.

Thousands of fans had prepared for the match by setting aside money for tickets, and those who did not get the chance to go to the stadium had planned to follow the match at the viewing kiosks that filled every corner of the city of Dar es Salaam and other large towns.

However, the sudden announcement of the postponement of the match shocked the owners of those kiosks, some of whom had already rented large televisions, added seats and even ordered enough drinks and food to serve their customers.

One of the kiosk owners in the Kinyerezi area, Juma Athumani, said he spent more than 150,000 improving his place, but did not manage to recover even a quarter of those costs after the match failed to take place.

"I rented a big screen and bought new speakers so that Yanga and Simba fans could enjoy the match, but now everything has been ruined. The money has been lost for nothing," he said, while another kiosk owner in the Mabibo area said he had paid for Azam decoders as well as buying drinks to sell during the match, but everything went wrong and he does not know who can ease his pain.

"It is true that even though the match has been postponed, the drinks and the decoders will remain, but it was not my aim to spend extra money on preparations for that match, and you know our Tanzanian incomes are patched together - you put out money by calculation in order to reap a profit, but things have turned sour for me. It hurts."

ENTREPRENEURS

A die-hard Yanga fan known by the name Jesca Manji said the postponement of the Yanga-Simba derby on March 8 plunged her into debts that nearly drove her to harm herself.

Jesca, who is in the business of selling food (a "mama lishe"), told Mwanaspoti that she went and took chickens from someone on credit, expecting that after the derby she would go and pay people their money, but things went wrong. "I took chickens worth 2 million shillings and I made all the business preparations, everything was ready, and surprisingly the Tanzania Premier League Board announced at 8:00 in the afternoon (2 p.m.) that there was no match. I found myself drained of strength, unable to know what to do, because the owner of the chickens wants his money, not words," said Jesca, and added:

"I found myself wanting to drink poison so I would die, but the thing that gave me strength is that I am a mother raising my children by myself; I thought about how they would live if I left this world, and I got the strength to keep fighting to see how I will pay people's debts."

She said that in a business of her kind, if she does not have a fridge to store them the chickens spoil, and that is what happened to many people on March 8, who found themselves throwing food away. "TFF and the League Board should have thought broadly in their decision; they know there are women traders who are fighting for their lives - let me keep quiet, because I am angry and I don't know what to do," said Jesca.

Other vendors alongside the Mkapa Stadium said they expected to make extra money through the derby as always happens when there is a big match, but found themselves suffering losses of food with no idea who would pay them those costs.

"It hurts a lot that a few people do things at their own whim, without caring about the losses suffered by those behind a big match like this; it is disrespecting the fans and football as a whole, because I hear that no postponement regulations were used, only decisions to protect one another - this is not right and it sets back the economy of individuals and even of the nation as a whole," said Hellen Muro, a food vendor.

THOSE FROM THE REGIONS

Getruda Emmanuel from Mafinga said this derby really punished them, because they travelled from Mafinga to Dar es Salaam in two coaster vehicles which they hired as a group of 60 fans in total, each one paying a fare of 60,000 shillings for the round trip.

Apart from the fare, Getruda explained that she paid for a place to sleep for two days, at 20,000 shillings a day.

"We contributed among ourselves, each one paid 60,000 shillings for the round-trip fare, we hired two vehicles and we were 60 fans. If you look at the costs of hiring all those vehicles, the total fare was three million six hundred thousand shillings," said Getruda.

Getruda said that for her part she spent in total more than 150,000 shillings including transport, food, accommodation and buying a jersey.

"Forget those costs; I am also a trader, I had to close my business for two days in order to come and watch this match, so I have not brought in anything and the thing I came for I missed," said Getruda, and added:

"Because of what is going on, I don't think that in future we fans from the regions will come to watch these derbies or any big match, because it has become uncertain whether it will be played - you can prepare and when you arrive there is no match."

YANGA NOW

Mwanaspoti sought out the Yanga leadership to find out the losses suffered by the club, which were the hosts, but their phones rang without being answered; however, an internal source from the club hinted to Mwanaspoti that the officials were in discussions and making an assessment of the matter.

"You cannot get them now, because they are in discussions and making a joint assessment to determine the full loss so that it can be put into the legal letter that will be sent to CAS, in order to claim the three points of the March 8 match as set out in the public statement," said the source, and added:

"There are big costs that were incurred starting from camp preparations, advertising and other things, so it is not easy to know them; that is why they are meeting now to settle it and then they will issue a statement, but the truth is that Yanga has suffered losses of millions of shillings because of the selfishness of a few."

Earlier, the Yanga Information Officer, Ally Kamwe, was quoted as saying that before the match was postponed more than 40,000 tickets had already been sold to fans, who nevertheless did not get the chance to witness the fixture because of the postponement by the League Board after Simba's threat to boycott.

Efforts to reach Simba officials and those of the League Board to obtain clarification on the losses they incurred in preparing for the match before it was postponed at short notice bore no fruit, as their phones rang without being answered.

The League Board are the chief organisers of the match, bearing the costs of servicing the match officials, including referees, commissioners and others, whether from Dar es Salaam or from the regions. This is the 13th time that Simba and Yanga have failed to face each other for various reasons in Mainland League matches since the league was founded in 1965, with records showing that Simba leads by having done so seven times against six for their rivals, and in recent years this is the second time a derby has been postponed within a short period, including that of May 8, 2021 when Yanga refused to play. That May 8 match was rescheduled to be played on July 3 that year and Yanga won 1-0 with a goal scored by Zawadi Mauya, while the match postponed at the weekend has still not been given a date and Yanga has already insisted it will not play it, saying it finished the job on March 8.

La ministre en charge du commerce et son homologue congolais ont officiellement lancé, le mercredi 30 octobre 2024 au poste-frontière de Gatumba, le Régime commercial simplifié (Recos) entre le république du Burundi et la République démocratique du Congo (RDC). Tous les services œuvrant dans les poste-frontières ont été appelés à tout faire pour que le Recos soit couronné de succès.
«L’objectif du Régime commercial simplifié est de promouvoir le développement du commerce transfrontalier en permettant aux petites marchandises de petits commerçants de bénéficier de l’élimination des droits de douane, d’un traitement préférentiel du Marché commun de l’Afrique orientale et australe (Comesa) sur les marchandises qui figurent sur la liste commune», a indiqué la ministre en charge du commerce, Marie Chantal Nijimbere, lors du lancement du Recos à Gatumba.
Mme Nijimbere a précisé que le Recos est un programme lancé par le Comesa en vue d’aider les petits commerçants transfrontaliers qui font le commerce de petites quantités de marchandises pour pouvoir orienter leurs activités dans le but de simplifier les processus de dédouanement et réduire les coûts de transactions commerciales.
Ainsi, soixante-dix marchandises produites dans les deux pays figurent déjà sur la liste commune. Mais, selon l’accord commercial signé entre les deux parties, la liste commune de produits n’est pas définitive et fera l’objet de révision tous les six mois en vue de l’auto-évaluation régulière dans un esprit de partenariat gagnant-gagnant, a laissé entendre Mme Nijimbere, avant d’appeler à l’augmentation de la production des produits concernés pour avoir la quantité suffisante à exporter en vue de tirer profit de ce Recos.
Le Recos vivement salué par les commerçants transfrontaliers
Le commerce transfrontalier est largement dominé par les femmes. Dans leurs témoignages, deux femmes burundaise et congolaise qui ont représenté celles qui font le commerce transfrontalier ont vivement salué le lancement du Recos, longtemps et impatiemment attendu. Ce dernier, ont-elles précisé, permettra de résoudre pas mal de défis auxquels elles faisaient face dans leur travail. En plus, le Recos permettra l’augmentation des recettes et un gain du temps. Ces femmes ont également demandé le suivi régulier de la mise en œuvre de ce Recos, la traduction des textes régissant ce régime en trois langues à savoir le Kirundi, le Français et le Swahili pour faciliter leur compréhension.
La ministre Nijimbere tout comme son homologue congolais en charge du commerce extérieur les ont tranquillisées, en leur promettant un suivi régulier, car ce Recos résulte de la volonté des plus hautes autorités des deux pays. Ces deux ministres ont ainsi appelé tous les services œuvrant aux poste-frontières à tout faire pour que la mise en œuvre de ce Régime commercial simplifié soit couronnée de succès.
Le lancement officiel du Recos s’est déroulé en présence de la délégation du Comesa, des autorités administratives des deux pays, etc. Avant le déroulement des cérémonies, une visite guidée a été effectuée dans les infrastructures érigées au poste-frontière des deux parties dans le cadre dudit projet.
Claude Hakizimana
a5419.en:
Burundi-DRC: Official launch of the Simplified Trade Regime

The minister in charge of trade and her Congolese counterpart officially launched, on Wednesday October 30, 2024 at the Gatumba border post, the Simplified Trade Regime (Recos) between the Republic of Burundi and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). All the services working at the border posts were called upon to do everything possible so that Recos is crowned with success.

"The objective of the Simplified Trade Regime is to promote the development of cross-border trade by allowing the small goods of small traders to benefit from the elimination of customs duties and from the preferential treatment of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) on the goods that appear on the common list," said the minister in charge of trade, Marie Chantal Nijimbere, at the launch of Recos in Gatumba.

Ms Nijimbere specified that Recos is a programme launched by Comesa with a view to helping small cross-border traders who trade in small quantities of goods, so that they can orient their activities with the aim of simplifying customs clearance processes and reducing the costs of commercial transactions.

Thus, seventy goods produced in the two countries already appear on the common list. But, according to the trade agreement signed between the two parties, the common list of products is not final and will be subject to revision every six months with a view to regular self-evaluation in a spirit of win-win partnership, Ms Nijimbere indicated, before calling for an increase in the production of the goods concerned in order to have sufficient quantities to export and thus benefit from this Recos.

Recos warmly welcomed by cross-border traders

Cross-border trade is largely dominated by women. In their testimonies, two women, one Burundian and one Congolese, who represented those engaged in cross-border trade, warmly welcomed the launch of Recos, long and impatiently awaited. The latter, they specified, will make it possible to resolve quite a few of the challenges they faced in their work. In addition, Recos will allow an increase in revenue and a saving of time. These women also requested regular monitoring of the implementation of this Recos, and the translation of the texts governing this regime into three languages, namely Kirundi, French and Swahili, to facilitate their understanding.

Minister Nijimbere, like her Congolese counterpart in charge of foreign trade, reassured them, promising them regular follow-up, because this Recos results from the will of the highest authorities of the two countries. The two ministers thus called on all the services working at the border posts to do everything possible so that the implementation of this Simplified Trade Regime is crowned with success.

The official launch of Recos took place in the presence of the Comesa delegation, the administrative authorities of the two countries, etc. Before the ceremonies took place, a guided tour was made of the infrastructure erected at the border post of the two parties within the framework of the said project.

Claude Hakizimana

a5435.t:
Il est difficile de croire qu’il s’agit de la même personne qui, il y a quinze jours, se tordait de douleur et d’inconfort dans l’unité d’isolement de l’hôpital général de Pallisa, dans l’est de l’Ouganda.
Anna avait été diagnostiquée avec la Mpox, une maladie virale que l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) a déclarée urgence de santé publique de portée internationale (USPI) le 14 août 2024. Au 18 décembre 2024, les rapports du ministère de la Santé montrent que 1 089 cas cumulés de mpox ont été confirmés en Ouganda.
Le 8 novembre 2024, Anna a commencé à ressentir un mal de tête et s’est rendue dans une clinique de Namuwongo, une banlieue de la ville de Kampala. Elle a reçu des analgésiques. « Je ressentais des douleurs corporelles, notamment dans les articulations. Parfois, je ressentais trop de chaleur dans mon corps. Mes yeux étaient rouges et je ne pouvais pas manger à cause des blessures dans ma bouche », se souvient Anna.
Après trois jours sans amélioration, Anna est retournée à la même clinique et a été testée positive au paludisme et aux ulcères. Elle a été traitée pour les deux maladies. Comme son état ne s’améliorait toujours pas, Anna a décidé de rentrer chez elle dans le village de Meitu, paroisse d’Obutet, sous-comté d’Obutet, district de Pallisa, pour être soignée par les membres de sa famille.
Cependant, à son retour à la maison, son état s’est aggravé. Elle souffrait trop. Les lésions sur son corps étaient douloureuses. Le frère d’Anna a emmené sa sœur dans une clinique voisine où elle a passé la nuit.
Testée positive au Mpox
perdu espoir.
L’hôpital général de Pallisa n’a pas de service d’isolement désigné. Le bureau de santé du district, avec le soutien de l’OMS, a improvisé en affectant une section du service pédiatrique à une unité d’isolement pour le Mpox avant la mise en place de l’unité actuelle de traitement du Mpox. Cela a fonctionné à l’avantage d’Anna car elle s’est fait des amis au-delà des agents de santé, y compris les soignants des enfants.
Anna a reçu un traitement gratuit et trois repas par jour grâce au gouvernement ougandais et à des partenaires, dont l’OMS, avec le soutien de l’Agence des Etats-Unis pour le développement international (USAID).
Avant la sortie d’Anna de l’établissement de santé, une équipe multidisciplinaire composée de la surveillance, de la communication des risques et de l’OMS a engagé les habitants du village de Meitu, d’où Anna est originaire, dans une séance de dialogue communautaire interactive de 45 minutes. La séance a porté sur la maladie du Mpox, ses causes, ses signes et symptômes, sa prévention et la nécessité d’informer les agents de santé du village ou l’établissement de santé le plus proche si quelqu’un présente des signes et des symptômes.
Au cours du dialogue, le responsable de la surveillance de la maladie du Mpox dans le district de Pallisa, Bernard Ikwaras, a souligné la nécessité d’éviter de stigmatiser les personnes atteintes de la maladie et les survivants.
« N’importe qui peut attraper le Mpox. Il est donc important qu’en tant que communauté, nous nous soutenions mutuellement. Lorsque les personnes se remettent du Mpox, elles ne peuvent plus propager la maladie, nous avons donc intérêt à les accueillir à nouveau dans la communauté », explique Bernard.
Le père d’Anna, Charles Otuna, a également assisté à la séance d’engagement communautaire. Le dialogue a dissipé les mythes pour garantir qu’Anna soit réintégrée dans la communauté, tout comme les 780 autres survivants en Ouganda.
« D’après l’expérience d’Anna, il est essentiel de sensibiliser davantage le public au Mpox et de veiller à ce que tous les agents de santé des centres de santé publics et privés du pays participent à des webinaires et à des séances de renforcement des capacités », explique le Dr Charles Njuguna, représentant par intérim de l’OMS en Ouganda.
« Cela facilitera le diagnostic rapide et le démarrage du traitement recommandé et d’autres interventions de contrôle pour arrêter la propagation du Mpox dans le pays ».
WN/as/fss/Sf/ac/APA
a5435.en:
Uganda: message of hope from an Mpox survivor

It is hard to believe that this is the same person who, a fortnight ago, was writhing in pain and discomfort in the isolation unit of Pallisa General Hospital, in eastern Uganda.

Anna had been diagnosed with Mpox, a viral disease that the World Health Organization (WHO) declared a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) on 14 August 2024. As of 18 December 2024, Ministry of Health reports show that 1,089 cumulative cases of mpox have been confirmed in Uganda.

On 8 November 2024, Anna began to feel a headache and went to a clinic in Namuwongo, a suburb of Kampala. She was given painkillers. “I had body aches, particularly in the joints. Sometimes I felt too much heat in my body. My eyes were red and I could not eat because of the sores in my mouth,” Anna recalls.

After three days without improvement, Anna returned to the same clinic and tested positive for malaria and ulcers. She was treated for both conditions. As her condition still did not improve, Anna decided to go home to the village of Meitu, Obutet parish, Obutet sub-county, Pallisa district, to be cared for by members of her family.

However, on her return home, her condition worsened. She was in too much pain. The lesions on her body were painful. Anna’s brother took his sister to a nearby clinic where she spent the night.

Tested positive for Mpox

[She had] lost hope.

Pallisa General Hospital has no designated isolation ward. The district health office, with WHO support, improvised by assigning a section of the paediatric ward as an isolation unit for Mpox before the current Mpox treatment unit was set up. This worked to Anna’s advantage as she made friends beyond the health workers, including the caregivers of the children.

Anna received free treatment and three meals a day thanks to the Ugandan government and partners, including WHO, with the support of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

Before Anna was discharged from the health facility, a multidisciplinary team made up of surveillance, risk communication and WHO staff engaged the residents of Meitu village, where Anna comes from, in an interactive 45-minute community dialogue session. The session covered Mpox disease, its causes, its signs and symptoms, its prevention, and the need to inform village health workers or the nearest health facility if someone shows signs and symptoms.

During the dialogue, the Mpox disease surveillance officer for Pallisa district, Bernard Ikwaras, stressed the need to avoid stigmatising people with the disease and survivors.

“Anyone can catch Mpox. It is therefore important that, as a community, we support one another. When people recover from Mpox, they can no longer spread the disease, so it is in our interest to welcome them back into the community,” Bernard explains.

Anna’s father, Charles Otuna, also attended the community engagement session. The dialogue dispelled myths to ensure that Anna is reintegrated into the community, just like the 780 other survivors in Uganda.

“From Anna’s experience, it is essential to raise more public awareness about Mpox and to ensure that all health workers in public and private health centres in the country take part in webinars and capacity-building sessions,” explains Dr Charles Njuguna, WHO acting representative in Uganda.

“This will facilitate rapid diagnosis and the start of the recommended treatment and other control interventions to stop the spread of Mpox in the country.”

WN/as/fss/Sf/ac/APA

a5603.t:
Ministry of Health says there are about 46 000 HIV-positive Malawians who do not know their status and are consequently not on antiretroviral therapy (ART), raising concerns about spread of new infections.
The ministry’s HIV and Viral Hepatitis Directorate deputy director Rabson Kachala said the figure is based on data captured during a quarterly supervision exercise conducted in March this year across 800 health facilities.
He said while 991 000 people in Malawi have tested HIV positive, only around 945 000 are currently accessing ART.
“This is a significant treatment gap. Many of the individuals who are not on ART fear stigma and discrimination which keeps them away from health facilities. This is a serious public health concern,” Kachala said.
Speaking on the sideline of a media workshop in Mponela, Dowa that focused on the recent donor funding freeze and the government’s strategies to sustain HIV services in the country, he also called for more aggressive public sensitisation to encourage people to know their HIV status and seek treatment early.
Kachala stressed that access to ART remains uninterrupted despite the ongoing restrictions on some donor-funded activities.
“There are misconceptions that ARVs are not available, but that is not true. These drugs are procured through the Global Fund and remain fully stocked. People should collect their medication on their scheduled dates without fear,” he said.
According to Kachala, the government has increased domestic financing for HIV programming in the 2025/26 financial year to K3.4 billion. This includes K1 billion for ART co-financing, K2.4 billion for sample transportation, and K500 million for capacity building.
Network of Journalists Living with HIV executive director David Kamkwamba appealed to the media to take an active role in raising public awareness about Malawi’s HIV response and the evolving funding landscape.
“The media must help break the silence and reduce stigma by consistently covering issues around HIV treatment, prevention and sustainable financing,” he said.
Kamkwamba said continued misinformation about ARV availability, coupled with low community engagement, risks eroding years of progress made in the fight against HIV in Malawi.
The ART treatment gap comes amid lingering aftershocks from a sweeping “stop work order” issued by USAid under US President Donald Trump, which froze funding for multiple health programmes in Malawi and has since had immediate and far-reaching consequences for community health services, especially HIV and Aids interventions.
In 2022, Minister of Health Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda announced that Malawi had surpassed the United Nations Aids Agency (UNAids) 95-95- 95 HIV epidemic control targets ahead of the deadline in June 2025.
The statistics show that Malawi is now at 94:99:95, meaning that 94 percent of all people with HIV are aware of their status, 99 percent of those aware of their status are on ART and 95 percent of those on antiretroviral treatment have achieved viral load suppression.

a5646.t:
- Hamas should accept a Gaza ceasefire, said US President Joe Biden.
- He warned that no truce deal in Ramadan could be dangerous.
- The US conducted food air drops in Gaza.
US President Joe Biden called on Hamas on Tuesday to accept a Gaza ceasefire deal by the Muslim holy month of Ramadan, while the Palestinian militant group warned talks for a truce and hostage release cannot go on "indefinitely".
As famine threatens Gazans, US and Jordanian planes again airdropped food aid into the besieged territory of 2.4 million people in a joint operation with Egypt and France.
US Vice President Kamala Harris has expressed "deep concern about the humanitarian conditions in Gaza", while the World Health Organisation (WHO) has reported children dying of starvation in two northern Gaza hospitals.
Envoys from Hamas and the US have been meeting Qatari and Egyptian mediators in Cairo for negotiations over a six-week truce, the exchange of dozens of remaining hostages for hundreds of Palestinian prisoners and the flow of aid to Gaza.
Egypt's Al-Qahera News, which is close to the country's intelligence services, said the talks would continue for a fourth consecutive day on Wednesday.
Biden warned Hamas to agree to a Gaza truce by Ramadan, which begins early next week, after his top diplomat Antony Blinken urged it to accept an "immediate ceasefire".
The US president told reporters from Maryland:
"There's got to be a ceasefire because Ramadan - if we get into circumstances where this continues to Ramadan, Israel and Jerusalem could be very, very dangerous."
He did not elaborate but the US urged Israel last week to allow Muslims to worship at the flashpoint Al-Aqsa mosque compound in Jerusalem during Ramadan.
The Israeli government said it would allow Muslim worshippers access to Al-Aqsa during Ramadan "in similar numbers to those in previous years".
The talks in Cairo have so far not included Israel, with Israeli media reporting that its delegates had boycotted the talks after Hamas failed to provide a list of living hostages.
However, senior Hamas leader Bassem Naim told AFP that details on the prisoners "were not mentioned in any documents or proposals circulated during the negotiation process".
DEVELOPING | Al-Aqsa access for Muslims same as in previous years, Israel says
Osama Hamdan, a Hamas official in Beirut, said his group would "not allow the path of negotiations to be open indefinitely".
Israel has said it believes 130 of the 250 captives taken by Hamas fighters in their unprecedented 7 October attack, which triggered the war, remain in Gaza but that 31 have been killed.
US National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met and agreed that "the release of sick, wounded, elderly, and women hostages would result in an immediate ceasefire in Gaza over a period of at least six weeks".
The first phase of a ceasefire would enable "a surge of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza and provide time and space to secure more enduring arrangements and sustained calm", a White House readout of the meeting said.
Israel is facing increasing criticism from its top ally the US as conditions in the besieged Palestinian territory deteriorate and famine looms.
Harris met Israeli war cabinet member Benny Gantz in Washington on Monday, the same day the WHO said an aid mission at the weekend found that 10 children had died of starvation at the Al-Awda and Kamal Adwan hospitals.
In Khan Yunis, the main city in Gaza's south, people described finding decomposing bodies lying in streets lined with destroyed buildings.
"We want to eat and live. Take a look at our homes. How am I to blame, a single, unarmed person without any income in this impoverished country?" said Nader Abu Shanab, pointing to the rubble with blackened hands.
American cargo planes airdropped more than 36 000 meals into Gaza on Tuesday in a joint operation with Jordan, which said French and Egyptian planes also took part.
The UN's World Food Programme said Israeli troops turned away an aid convoy at a checkpoint leading to northern Gaza and that it was later looted "by desperate people".
The Hamas attack on southern Israel on 7 October resulted in about 1 160 deaths, most of them civilians, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
Israel's retaliatory offensive has killed more than 30 600 people, mostly women and children, according to the health ministry in the Hamas-ruled territory.
Tensions have flared between Israel and the UN over the handling of allegations of sexual assault by Hamas militants during the October attack.
The UN published a report on Monday that said there were "reasonable grounds to believe" rapes were committed and that hostages taken to Gaza had also been raped.
Israel has accused the UN of taking too long to respond to the claims and recalled its UN Ambassador Gilad Erdan shortly after the report's release.
The war has sparked violence across the region, including near-daily exchanges of fire between Israeli forces and Lebanon's Hezbollah movement.
The US military said it shot down three drones and a missile fired toward one of its destroyers in the Red Sea Huthi rebels in Yemen on Tuesday.
A statement by US Central Command said "one anti-ship ballistic missile and three one-way attack unmanned aerial systems" had been shot down and that its ship, the USS Carney, was undamaged.
Iran-backed Houthis have been attacking shipping in the Red Sea for months, saying they were hitting Israel-linked vessels in support of Palestinians in Gaza.
Anger over Israel's Gaza campaign has grown across the Middle East, stoking violence involving Iran-backed groups in Lebanon, Iraq, Syria and Yemen.

a5743.t:
The Attorney General (A-G), Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine, has dismissed claims that President John Dramani Mahama influenced his decision to discontinue several high-profile criminal cases.
Since assuming office last month, Dr. Ayine has terminated cases involving key state officials, including Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson and Bank of Ghana Governor Dr. Johnson Asiama.
Speaking at a press conference in Accra on Wednesday, February 12, Dr. Ayine clarified that these decisions were made independently by his office after a thorough professional review of the cases. He emphasized that President Mahama played no role in the discontinuation of any case.
"Ladies and gentlemen, my decision to terminate the criminal trials was animated in the main by three factors. The first was that for ethical and professional reasons, I could not in good conscience continue to prosecute some of the cases," he said.
"The second was that, for some of the cases, my own review and analysis of the charges showed clearly that the charges were defective, and some were filed against the promptings of plain commonsense."
He continued: "The third reason was that, in some of the cases, the evidence led so far showed that there was reasonable doubt as to the guilt of the accused persons, and no prosecutor should continue to pursue a case in the face of overwhelming doubt regarding the guilt of the accused."
Dr. Ayine explained that before reaching these decisions, he conducted extensive consultations, including multiple briefings with the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) and discussions with defense lawyers involved in the cases.
He further noted that in cases where disagreements arose—such as those related to the banking sector clean-up—he communicated his views directly to the lawyers involved.
"As Attorney General, I am keenly aware that the prosecutorial authority vested in me under Article 88 of the Constitution is discretionary in nature and is subject to the constitutional requirements set out in Article 296 of the Constitution."
He added that the Constitution mandates him to act fairly, reasonably, and without bias, stating: "The import of these constitutional requirements is that, in the exercise of my prosecutorial power, I must not only act reasonably and fairly and comply with all the requirements imposed on me by law but also, I must be candid with those whose life and liberty depend on my decisions."
Dropped cases
The Attorney-General’s decision affected seven major cases, including that of former Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana, now Acting Governor, Johnson Asiama, whose charges related to the collapse of UniBank and UT Bank were withdrawn.
The A-G also dropped charges against Finance Minister Ato Forson and businessman Richard Jakpa in the controversial ambulance procurement case.
Additionally, the trial of former COCOBOD CEO, Dr. Stephen Kwabena Opuni, and businessman Seidu Agongo, accused of causing GH¢271 million in financial loss through the Lithovit foliar fertiliser scandal, was discontinued.
In another high-profile decision, the A-G withdrew charges against former SSNIT boss Dr. Ernest Thompson and three others accused of financial mismanagement, though he noted that some persons linked to SSNIT and the banking sector cases were still standing trial.
The financial misconduct trial of former Works and Housing Minister Collins Dauda and four others in the Saglemi Housing Project was also discontinued through a nolle prosequi.
Other notable cases dropped include those against activist Oliver Barker-Vormawor, Ama Governor, and others, reigniting debates on protest rights and political suppression. Additionally, former NDC Chairman Samuel Ofosu Ampofo and Communications Officer Anthony Kwaku Boahen were freed from charges related to a leaked recording allegedly plotting political violence.
Dr. Ayine maintains that his decisions were legally and ethically sound, reiterating that justice, not politics, guided his actions.

a5764.t:
Suspendue depuis 2011 après le raid solitaire des forces spéciales américaines qui a tué Ben Laden, l’aide antiterroriste des Etats-Unis au Pakistan est sur le point d’être rétablie. C’est du moins ce que l’on peut retenir de la visite officielle aux Etats-Unis du premier ministre Pakistanais, Nawaz Sharif ce dimanche 20 octobre.
Une visite au cours de laquelle, le premier ministre Nawaz Sharif a eu un entretien et un diner privés avec John Kerry, le Secrétaire d’Etat américain. C’est d’ailleurs Marie Harf, l’une des porte-parole du Secrétariat d’Etat qui donne les détails de ce probable reprise de l’aide.
Marie Harf a rappelé qu’au cours de l’été passé, le département d’Etat a notifié au Congrès comment il comptait financer certains programme au Pakistan. Et cela, dans le cadre d’un long processus de « redémarrage de notre assistance en matière de sécurité ». D’une valeur de trois cent cinquante(350) millions de dollars, cette assistance financière antiterroriste permet de développer « les capacités des forces de sécurité du Pakistan en matière de contre-insurrection et d’anti-terrorisme », a ajouté la porte-parole. Qui précise : « Pour l’année budgétaire 2014, le président a demandé au Congrès une aide étrangère au Pakistan d’un montant de 1, 162 milliard de dollars, dont 857 millions d’aide civile et 305 millions d’assistance sécuritaire ».
De quoi réchauffer la relation teintée de controverses qu’entretiennent les deux « alliés » depuis 2001 dans la guerre de Washington contre le terrorisme.
a5764.en:
Suspended since 2011 after the solo raid by American special forces that killed Bin Laden, US counterterrorism aid to Pakistan is about to be restored. That, at least, is what can be drawn from the official visit to the United States of Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif this Sunday, 20 October.

During the visit, Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif had a private meeting and dinner with John Kerry, the American Secretary of State. It is in fact Marie Harf, one of the State Department’s spokespersons, who gives the details of this likely resumption of the aid.

Marie Harf recalled that over the past summer, the State Department notified Congress of how it intended to fund certain programmes in Pakistan. And this, as part of a long process of “restarting our security assistance”. Worth three hundred and fifty (350) million dollars, this counterterrorism financial assistance serves to develop “the capacities of Pakistan’s security forces in counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism”, the spokesperson added. She specified: “For budget year 2014, the president asked Congress for foreign aid to Pakistan in the amount of 1.162 billion dollars, of which 857 million is civilian aid and 305 million is security assistance.”

Enough to warm up the controversy-tinged relationship that the two “allies” have maintained since 2001 in Washington’s war on terror.

a5805.t:
Une fois encore, le réalisateur béninois vivant en France, Sylvestre Amoussou, était à l’honneur, vendredi 4 avril 2025, à l’espace culturel Le Centre. C’était à travers la projection sur grand écran de son long-métrage » Un pas en avant : les dessous de la corruption « .
Après » L’orage africain, un continent sous influence » projeté en fin d’année 2024, Sylvestre Amoussou revient encore sur les écrans de l’espace culturel Le Centre avec » Un pas en avant : les dessous de la corruption « , un long-métrage de 1h 45mn qui dépeint les contours de la corruption, fléau qui gangrène le développement de l’Afrique. Le synopsis parle de la disparition d’un petit artisan. Son frère épicier, dans sa quête de savoir ce qui s’est passé, tombe sur un dossier de détournement de l’aide humanitaire. Il découvre que des gens se remplissent les poches, commettent des crimes, usent de menaces et intimidations pour s’en sortir. Mais le petit épicier est bien décidé à aller au bout. Avec » Un pas en avant : les dessous de la corruption » Sylvestre Amoussou est dans un rôle qu’il affectionne le plus, éduquer, dénoncer les maux qui minent le continent africain. Il y a fait jouer des acteurs béninois et étrangers, utilisant des noms comme Godomey, Calavi, etc. Intervenant en direct de la France, à la fin de la projection, Sylvestre Amoussou justifie cela par la nécessité de faire connaître les villes béninoises au-delà des frontières. « …quand je parle de l’aide humanitaire, je montre que même les aides qu’ils donnent pour le continent africain, il y a une partie qui est déjà détournée même par les donateurs avant d’arriver. Et quand ils arrivent en Afrique, nos gouvernements détournent une grosse partie et les gens pour qui c’est destiné n’ont pas grand-chose. C’est un éveil de conscience pour parler de bonne gouvernance, ce qui est vraiment très difficile, que ce soit chez nous, que ce soit ailleurs » a laissé entendre Sylvestre Amoussou.
Pour Berthold Hinkati, le Directeur de l’espace culturel Le Centre, ce sont les échos favorables reçus sur le film qui ont pesé pour son choix. « Il y avait la qualité et ça dénonçait des phénomènes sociaux. Ce qui entre bien en lien avec le programme Wà Cinéma. D’où l’idée d’une projection avec ce même réalisateur qui fait honneur à l’Afrique et au Bénin. Les réalisateurs en général profitent de la fiction pour véhiculer de très bons messages. Et ce soir, nous avons entendu de très bonnes informations liées à la corruption. On a réellement vu les dessous de la corruption » a souligné Berthold Hinkati.
Usager de l’espace culturel Le Centre, Joël Hossou est satisfait. A ses dires, ce n’est pas facile de traiter ce genre de sujet. Il a fallu à Sylvestre Amoussou beaucoup d’audace et de courage, fait-il observer. « Le film a été tourné en 2010 et avec cette qualité-là, j’imagine qu’il doit reprendre un pareil projet en ce moment. Je crois que ce sera une très bonne qualité. J’espère que les gens ont appris du film et vivement que la corruption diminue dans les communautés africaines » souhaite-t-il.
Réalisateur, Terrence Anago affirme apprécier la technique, l’histoire, la dramaturgie. A ses dires, c’est toujours un plaisir de venir visionner des œuvres de qualité à l’espace culturel Le Centre.
Bertrand HOUANHO
a5805.en:
Once again, the Beninese director living in France, Sylvestre Amoussou, was honoured on Friday 4 April 2025 at the cultural space Le Centre. This was through the big-screen showing of his feature film “Un pas en avant: les dessous de la corruption” (A Step Forward: The Underside of Corruption).
After “L'orage africain, un continent sous influence”, screened at the end of 2024, Sylvestre Amoussou returns to the screens of the cultural space Le Centre with “Un pas en avant: les dessous de la corruption”, a 1 hour 45 minute feature film that depicts the contours of corruption, the scourge that eats away at Africa's development. The synopsis tells of the disappearance of a small craftsman. His grocer brother, in his quest to find out what happened, comes across a file on the embezzlement of humanitarian aid. He discovers that people are lining their pockets, committing crimes, using threats and intimidation to get away with it. But the little grocer is determined to go all the way. With “Un pas en avant: les dessous de la corruption”, Sylvestre Amoussou is in the role he most cherishes: educating, denouncing the ills that undermine the African continent. He cast Beninese and foreign actors, using names such as Godomey, Calavi, etc. Speaking live from France at the end of the screening, Sylvestre Amoussou justified this by the need to make Beninese towns known beyond the borders. “...when I speak of humanitarian aid, I show that even the aid they give for the African continent, part of it is already embezzled by the donors before it arrives. And when it arrives in Africa, our governments embezzle a large part and the people it is meant for get very little. It is a wake-up call to speak about good governance, which is really very difficult, whether at home or elsewhere,” said Sylvestre Amoussou.
For Berthold Hinkati, the Director of the cultural space Le Centre, it was the favourable feedback received about the film that weighed in its selection. “There was quality and it denounced social phenomena. That fits well with the Wà Cinéma programme. Hence the idea of a screening with this same director who does honour to Africa and to Benin. Directors in general take advantage of fiction to convey very good messages. And this evening we heard very good information about corruption. We really saw the underside of corruption,” stressed Berthold Hinkati.
A user of the cultural space Le Centre, Joël Hossou, is satisfied. In his words, it is not easy to deal with this kind of subject. It took Sylvestre Amoussou a great deal of daring and courage, he observes. “The film was shot in 2010 and with that quality, I imagine he must take up a similar project now. I believe it will be of very good quality. I hope people have learned from the film and may corruption diminish in African communities,” he wishes.
Director Terrence Anago says he appreciates the technique, the story, the dramaturgy. In his words, it is always a pleasure to come and view quality works at the cultural space Le Centre.
Bertrand HOUANHO

a6045.t:
Namibia is still among the countries that are committed to ending AIDS by 2030.
This ambitious goal is being strengthened at a two-day workshop focused on the Sustainability Roadmap and the National Operational Plan, which will outline a comprehensive pathway towards sustained epidemic control of HIV, TB, malaria, and hepatitis.
The Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services, Ben Nangombe, reiterated that Namibia has made commendable progress in curbing the spread of infectious diseases like HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria.
"We have witnessed significant forward movement in achieving the goals articulated in the National Strategic Framework, thanks in large part to the invaluable support by our Development Cooperation Partners and the active role of Civil Society Organisations (CSOs). The data and figures towards Namibia's achievements of the UNAIDS 95-95-95 fast-tracked targets for HIV are well known to all of you. As of 2022 in Namibia, 94% of HIV-positive individuals know their status, 97% of them are on antiretroviral therapy (ART), and 93% have reached viral suppression (94-97-93)."
The National Operational Plan and Sustainability Roadmap are seen as critical in the final push to eradicate AIDS and other diseases as public health threats by 2030.
The Sustainability Roadmap and National Operational Plan will be launched during this year's World AIDS Day commemoration on the 1st of December.
"This is the last mile, and we dare not relent. We will not falter. Not now, when we have achieved so much. Let us maintain the momentum and deliver a solid NOP and a comprehensive sustainability framework to operationalise our NSF for HIV, TB, malaria, and hepatitis."
PEPFAR Representative Cheryl Amoroso discussed the funding perspective of PEPFAR as a donor.
"From a PEPFAR perspective, we need to already embrace change to together understand the transformation of HIV programming in line with this developing vision that the country has for its future health system, not just from an HIV perspective but holistically. From a donor viewpoint, we are ready to adapt our investments to help realise this developing vision, which is why today and tomorrow are so important. We will use this roadmap to guide our investment. The Namibia PEPFAR investments have already started making shifts better aligned with the future vision that is already developing, and the clarity that we will have on this documentation will continue to support that transition."

a6142.t:
Le président malawite a concédé sa défaite aux élections générales du 16 septembre, félicitant son successeur et répondant aux appels des personnalités nationales pour une transition pacifique.
Le président malawite Lazarus Chakwera a reconnu ce mercredi sa défaite aux élections générales du 16 septembre et a félicité son prédécesseur Peter Mutharika, chef de l’opposition et candidat du Parti démocratique progressiste (DPP), qui lui succède. Chakwera n’effectuera ainsi qu’un seul mandat à la tête du pays.
S’exprimant depuis le palais Kamuzu à Lilongwe, il a admis que Mutharika disposait d’une avance qu’il a qualifiée d’« insurmontable » après le dépouillement de 24 conseils, alors qu’il n’en restait que 12.
« Il y a un instant, j’ai appelé directement le professeur Mutharika pour le féliciter de sa victoire historique et lui souhaiter bonne chance en tant que nouveau président de la République du Malawi », a-t-il déclaré.
Appelant à l’unité nationale, le chef de l’État sortant a invité tous les citoyens, quelles que soient leurs appartenances politiques, à se rallier au président élu. Cette concession intervient après les appels répétés de personnalités nationales, parmi lesquelles le Conseil des églises du Malawi (MCC) et l’ancien président Bakili Muluzi, qui ont plaidé pour l’acceptation des résultats afin de préserver la paix et la stabilité démocratique.
Le président du MCC, Billy Gamah, avait affirmé qu’une concession rapide constituerait « un geste d’homme d’État » favorisant le calme et la maturité parmi les partisans, tandis que Muluzi avait encouragé Chakwera à « laisser le pays aller de l’avant » et rappelé qu’« il y a une vie après le Palais présidentiel ».
Selon les chiffres provisoires publiés par la Commission électorale (MEC), Peter Mutharika recueillait environ 66 % des suffrages valides, contre 24 % pour Lazarus Chakwera, avec 205 480 bulletins déclarés nuls, soit 3,45 %. Les résultats définitifs de la présidentielle sont attendus ce mercredi, ceux des élections législatives le 30 septembre, tandis que les résultats des conseillers locaux doivent être proclamés dans les deux prochaines semaines.
JN/fss/ac/Sf/APA
a6142.en:
The Malawian president conceded defeat in the general elections of 16 September, congratulating his successor and responding to calls from national figures for a peaceful transition.

Malawian President Lazarus Chakwera on Wednesday acknowledged his defeat in the general elections of 16 September and congratulated his predecessor Peter Mutharika, leader of the opposition and candidate of the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), who succeeds him. Chakwera will thus serve only a single term at the head of the country.

Speaking from the Kamuzu Palace in Lilongwe, he admitted that Mutharika held a lead he described as "insurmountable" after the counting of 24 councils, with only 12 remaining.

"A moment ago, I called Professor Mutharika directly to congratulate him on his historic victory and to wish him good luck as the new president of the Republic of Malawi," he declared.

Calling for national unity, the outgoing head of state invited all citizens, whatever their political affiliations, to rally behind the president-elect. This concession comes after repeated appeals from national figures, among them the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and former president Bakili Muluzi, who pleaded for the results to be accepted in order to preserve peace and democratic stability.

The president of the MCC, Billy Gamah, had stated that a rapid concession would constitute "an act of statesmanship" fostering calm and maturity among supporters, while Muluzi had encouraged Chakwera to "let the country move forward" and recalled that "there is life after the Presidential Palace."

According to provisional figures published by the Electoral Commission (MEC), Peter Mutharika was gathering around 66% of valid votes, against 24% for Lazarus Chakwera, with 205,480 ballots declared void, that is 3.45%. The definitive results of the presidential election are expected this Wednesday, those of the legislative elections on 30 September, while the results for local councillors are to be proclaimed within the next two weeks.

JN/fss/ac/Sf/APA

DAR ES SALAAM: The USAID’s Afya Yangu Southern and USAID Kizazi Hodari Southern Zone projects funded by PEPFAR/USAID and implemented by Deloitte Consulting Limited joined WiLDAF Tanzania to launch the campaign of 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence (GBV).
This year’s campaign will be heralded by the theme: ‘Towards 30 Years Beijing, Unite to end Violence against Women and Girls”.
The campaign marks the 30th anniversary review of the implementation of the Beijing Declaration and Platform for action.
The 16-day celebration of sexual violence in 2024, with this year’s slogan being ‘After 30 years of Beijing, let’s unite to eradicate violence against women and girls.
Speaking in Dar es Salaam early Sunday ( December 1, 2024), when the campaign was launched, representative from the USAID Afya Yangu Southern Zone project, Jackline Uwaya said that the community has a great contribution in the fight to eradicate and end gender violence.
“Together we have the ability to influence the society mindset towards gender violence, as people take time to think deeply about any information about acts of gender-based violence when they occur,” said Uwaya.
She added that if members of society, government and other stakeholders join forces, GBV will end.
However, she said that currently Tanzania has been able to take major steps in the fight against gender violence compared to previous years, thanks to the cooperation between the government and private institutions.
Speaking at the same event, chief guest Ambassador Getrude Mongela said that if society is properly educated about the effects of gender based violence, it will refrain from such actions.
“These acts of violence against gender occur in the society in which we all live. If we invest a lot on promoting education and we all join together, these actions can end completely,” said Ambassador Mongela.
According to the gender activist, it is possible to have a zero gender based violence society hence members of community should join forces in GBV fighs.
“Everyone should fulfill their responsibility in ensuring that sexual violence is eradicated,” she insisted.

a6474.t:
The Namibian government says the imposition of reciprocal tariffs by the US President, Donald Trump, requires a balanced approach from Southern African Customs Union member states, including Namibia, to find a workable solution.
This is in response to the 21% tariffs imposed by the Trump administration on Namibia as part of a series of sweeping reciprocal tariffs on U.S. trade partners.
The statement from the Ministry of International Relations and Trade says that to mitigate the impact of the tariffs imposed, stakeholder engagements will be imperative to gauge and establish the extent of the effects imposed by the U.S.
"It is also worth noting that the imposition of tariffs could lead to decreased competitiveness of Namibian beef and fish exports in the U.S. market, potentially reducing sales volume and demand for Namibian products due to price increases attributed to the tariff. Overall, the tariffs could disrupt established supply chains and negatively affect Namibia's export earnings, impacting broader preferential stability for Namibian products under the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) regime," the statement reads.
Namibia imposes a 42% tariff on goods imported from the U.S., which the ministry labels as maybe a contributing factor to President Trump's decision.
However, it added that not all goods from the USA into Namibia attract customs duties as per the SACU tariff structure.

a6476.t:
Après des conversations communautaires avec les femmes du Nord Bénin, dans le cadre du projet : « Prenez la parole : Développer les efforts de plaidoyer des femmes du Nord en matière de sécurité », financé par l’USAID/PRAPC, la Plateforme des organisations béninoises pour les droits des femmes (WROP BENIN) a procédé hier, mercredi 6 novembre 2024, à la présentation des points de plaidoyers aux institutions et aux partenaires techniques et financiers.
Pendant 5 mois, la Plateforme des organisations béninoises pour les droits des femmes (WROP BENIN) a parcouru 12 communes, 77 arrondissements dans les départements de l’Alibori, la Donga et l’Atacora. Elle a tenu avec les femmes, avec le concours du Caucus des femmes parlementaires, des conversations en langue locale, des discussions de groupes, des séances de renforcement de capacités sur des concepts liés à la sécurité et la paix. A la fin, il a été adopté à Parakou un plan d’action. Ce sont donc ces résultats qui ont été présentés lors d’un atelier de restitution aux partenaires et institutions afin que des décisions soient prises pour répondre aux besoins exprimés par les femmes du Nord en matière de sécurité.
Dans son allocution, la présidente de Wrop Bénin, Falola Djogbénou Venise, a laissé entendre que les résultats tournent autour de trois axes de plaidoyer que sont la cohésion sociale et vivre ensemble pacifiquement, l’employabilité, l’autonomisation et la contribution à l’économie locale, femme, la promotion politico-administrative, la participation à la gouvernance et au développement local. « Je me réjouis de la présentation des résultats desdits travaux afin que les prochaines actions puissent s’inscrire dans le dynamique de relever un défi majeur, celui de jouer un rôle déterminant dans l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre des lois et politiques importantes relatives à l’équité, voire à l’égalité du genre ou de sexe, à l’autonomisation de la femme et à sa représentativité dans toutes les instances de prise de décision » a-t-elle souligné.
A sa suite, la présidente du Caucus des femmes parlementaires, Djamilatou Sabi Mohamed, a situé l’apport des femmes parlementaires à trois niveaux. Il s’agit d’abord pour elles de prendre part aux séances de conversations communautaires avec 308 femmes leaders. En deuxième lieu, il y a eu l’atelier d’harmonisation qui s’est tenu à Parakou portant sur l’élaboration du plan de plaidoyer des femmes communautaires au cours duquel une feuille de route de mise en œuvre du plan a été élaborée et validée. En matière d’engagements pris par les femmes parlementaires, il y a des questions d’actualité au gouvernement, des initiatives de prise de loi, la mise sur pied de Commission d’information, de résolutions et d’enquêtes parlementaires en rapport avec la préoccupation des femmes sur les questions sécuritaires. Le 3e niveau d’intervention est la participation du Caucus à l’atelier de restitution.
Quant à la représentante de l’USAID, Abigail Slenski, elle a expliqué que OTI Programme régional d’appui aux pays côtiers (PRAPC) a pour objectif de renforcer la cohésion sociale et soutenir les communautés pour limiter leur vulnérabilité face à la situation de sécurité actuelle. « Le PRAPC travaille avec les autorités au niveau national et local. Il collabore également plus étroitement avec les organisations de la société civile, les associations des jeunes et des femmes en apportant un soutien financier et technique à leurs actions et initiatives à fort impact en vue de renforcer la paix et la cohésion sociale », a-t-elle laissé entendre.
Déclarant ouverts les travaux, le Préfet du Littoral, Alain Orounla, a fait le plaidoyer que le projet soit élargi au département du Littoral et que les hommes également soient pris en compte.
Bertrand HOUANHO
a6476.en:
Following community conversations with the women of northern Benin, as part of the project "Speak Up: Developing the advocacy efforts of northern women on security matters", funded by USAID/PRAPC, the Platform of Beninese Organisations for Women's Rights (WROP BENIN) yesterday, Wednesday 6 November 2024, presented its advocacy points to institutions and to technical and financial partners.

Over five months, the Platform of Beninese Organisations for Women's Rights (WROP BENIN) travelled through 12 communes and 77 districts in the departments of Alibori, Donga and Atacora. With the support of the Caucus of Women Parliamentarians, it held conversations with women in local languages, group discussions, and capacity-building sessions on concepts related to security and peace. At the end, an action plan was adopted in Parakou. It was these results that were presented at a feedback workshop for partners and institutions so that decisions could be taken to respond to the needs expressed by the women of the North on security matters.

In her address, the president of WROP Benin, Falola Djogbenou Venise, indicated that the results revolve around three advocacy priorities: social cohesion and peaceful coexistence; employability, empowerment and contribution to the local economy; and women's political and administrative advancement, participation in governance and in local development. "I am delighted by the presentation of the results of this work, so that the next actions can be part of the drive to meet a major challenge: that of playing a decisive role in drafting and implementing important laws and policies relating to gender equity, and indeed equality, to women's empowerment and to their representation in all decision-making bodies," she stressed.

Following her, the president of the Caucus of Women Parliamentarians, Djamilatou Sabi Mohamed, set out the contribution of women parliamentarians at three levels. First, it is for them to take part in the community conversation sessions with 308 women leaders. Second, there was the harmonisation workshop held in Parakou on drawing up the community women's advocacy plan, during which a roadmap for implementing the plan was drafted and validated. As for the commitments made by the women parliamentarians, these include topical questions to the government, legislative initiatives, and the setting up of parliamentary information, resolution and inquiry commissions relating to women's concerns on security issues. The third level of intervention is the Caucus's participation in the feedback workshop.

As for the USAID representative, Abigail Slenski, she explained that the OTI Regional Coastal Countries Support Programme (PRAPC) aims to strengthen social cohesion and support communities in limiting their vulnerability in the face of the current security situation. "PRAPC works with the authorities at national and local level. It also works more closely with civil society organisations and youth and women's associations, providing financial and technical support to their high-impact actions and initiatives in order to strengthen peace and social cohesion," she said.

Declaring the proceedings open, the Prefect of Littoral, Alain Orounla, advocated that the project be extended to the Littoral department and that men also be taken into account.

Bertrand HOUANHO
